chunks.title: Topical & local anaesthetics
chunks.tldr: Topical: proparacaine 0.5% (onset 20 s, least irritating — best for culture scrapes), tetracaine 0.5% (stings, 15–20 min), benoxinate 0.4% + fluorescein (tonometry), lidocaine 3.5% gel, cocaine. Never prescribe for home use. Injectable: short — lidocaine (fast, 1–2 h; max 4.5 mg/kg plain, 7 mg/kg with adrenaline), mepivacaine (lidocaine allergy), ropivacaine; long — bupivacaine (6–10 h; max 150 mg ≈ 20 mL 0.75%), levobupivacaine. Adrenaline ≤1:200,000 (arrhythmia). Hyaluronidase speeds spread (peribulbar). Peribulbar/sub-Tenon 5–10 mL (max 15). Intracameral anaesthetic/mydriatic must be preservative-free.

chunks.title: Mydriatics & cycloplegics
chunks.tldr: Phenylephrine (α-agonist, mydriasis only): 2.5%/10%; avoid 10% in neonates, cardiac patients, MAOI/TCA/reserpine/guanethidine. Antimuscarinics (dilate + cycloplegia), shortest → longest: tropicamide (peak 20–25 min, recovery 5–6 h; weak cycloplegia — fundus exam) < cyclopentolate (<24 h; refraction; neurotoxic in kids — hallucinations, ataxia) < homatropine (36–48 h; uveitis) < scopolamine/hyoscine (3–5 days; confusion in elderly) < atropine (up to 2 weeks; refraction in ET/dark irides, uveitis; toxicity — hot, dry, flushed, tachycardic, delirious). Cyclomydril (cyclopentolate 0.2% + phenylephrine 1%) for premature infants; Mydrasert insert; Mydrane intracameral (phenylephrine + tropicamide + lidocaine). Caution in narrow angles.
chunks.hook: Duration ladder: Tropicamide → Cyclopentolate → Homatropine → Scopolamine → Atropine.

cards.q: Which cycloplegic lasts up to two weeks?
Why avoid phenylephrine 10% in some patients?
cards.a: Systemic vasopressor effects — hypertension/arrhythmia, especially in neonates, cardiac patients, or those on TCAs, MAOIs, reserpine or guanethidine.

chunks.title: Glaucoma drug formulary
chunks.tldr: PGAs (nightly): latanoprost 0.005%, travoprost 0.004%, bimatoprost 0.03%, tafluprost 0.0015% (PF); unoprostone bd — ↑uveoscleral; iris darkening, lashes, periorbital fat atrophy, hyperaemia, CME/uveitis. β-blockers: timolol 0.25/0.5% (gel once daily), levobunolol, carteolol, metipranolol; betaxolol (β1, weaker). α2: apraclonidine 1% around laser (0.5% short-term; tachyphylaxis, lid retraction, blanching); brimonidine 0.2% (allergy, dry mouth; minimal CVS). Topical CAI: dorzolamide 2%, brinzolamide 1% (tds alone, bd add-on; bitter taste). Cholinergics: pilocarpine 1–4% (avoid in uveitis), carbachol; intracameral miochol/miostat. Combos: Cosopt, Combigan, Simbrinza, Xalacom, Duotrav, Ganfort. Acetazolamide 125–250 mg qds / SR 250–500 mg / 500 mg IV (max 1 g/d; IIH up to 4 g) — K⁺ loss, acidosis, stones, paraesthesia, SJS; methazolamide (HLA-B*59 SJS in Han Chinese). Osmotics: oral glycerol 1–1.5 g/kg, isosorbide 1.5 g/kg (no sugar), IV mannitol 1.5–2 g/kg (fluid overload), urea.
chunks.hook: Glycerol raises sugar; isosorbide doesn't; mannitol floods the heart.

cards.q: Which α2-agonist is mainly used to prevent IOP spikes after anterior segment laser?

cards.a: Oral isosorbide (no calories or glucose rise).

chunks.title: Steroids, NSAIDs & anti-allergy drops
chunks.tldr: Topical steroid potency: prednisolone 4× hydrocortisone, dexamethasone/betamethasone 25×; options: prednisolone acetate 1% (shake), dexamethasone 0.1%, FML, rimexolone, loteprednol (less IOP rise). Risks: microbial/HSV keratitis, steroid glaucoma, PSC cataract → ophthalmologist only. Steroid-antibiotic combos only when both truly indicated. NSAIDs: oral indomethacin/flurbiprofen/ibuprofen first-line for non-necrotising scleritis; topical diclofenac, flurbiprofen (pre-op miosis prevention), ketorolac (allergy, post-op; Omidria intracameral with phenylephrine), nepafenac, bromfenac (post-op inflammation, CME). Allergy: antihistamines (emedastine, levocabastine), mast-cell stabilisers (cromolyn, lodoxamide, nedocromil, pemirolast — slow onset), dual (olopatadine, ketotifen, epinastine, azelastine, bepotastine, alcaftadine); OTC decongestants (naphazoline, tetrahydrozoline) → rebound. Ciclosporin 0.05% bd (dry eye, VKC/AKC, grafts); tacrolimus ointment.
chunks.hook: Steroid drop = check pressure, check for herpes.

chunks.title: Antibacterials
chunks.tldr: Topical sulfonamides (cheap, broad, low allergy). Avoid topical use of key systemic antibiotics where possible (resistance, sensitisation). Fluoroquinolones (cipro, oflox, levo 1.5%, moxi, gati, besifloxacin) = first choice for ulcers; keratitis regimen hourly by day + 2-hourly night ×48 h then taper. Fortified: gentamicin/tobramycin 1.5% (tobra better for strep & Pseudomonas), cefuroxime/cefazolin 5%, ceftazidime 5%, amikacin 2.5%. Chloramphenicol (broad; rare aplastic anaemia), fusidic acid bd (staph), azithromycin 1%, erythromycin ointment (neonatal prophylaxis), tetracycline (chlamydia), bacitracin (G+), polymyxin B (G–, combined with trimethoprim/bacitracin), neomycin (contact allergy 5%). Propamidine (Acanthamoeba). Intracameral cefuroxime 1 mg after cataract surgery.

chunks.title: Intravitreal & antifungal/antiviral doses
chunks.tldr: Endophthalmitis (intravitreal, 0.1 mL, preservative-free): vancomycin 1 mg + ceftazidime 2.25 mg (or amikacin 0.4 mg); antifungals amphotericin 5–10 µg, voriconazole 0.1 mg; antivirals ganciclovir 2 mg (or 4.5 mg implant), foscarnet 1.2–2.4 mg; clindamycin 1 mg (toxo). Systemic adds benefit for endogenous/traumatic, not post-surgical. Topical antifungals: natamycin 5% (first choice keratitis), amphotericin 0.1–0.5%, voriconazole 1%, other azoles (compounded). Antivirals: acyclovir oral 800 mg 5×/d HZO; 400–800 mg 3–5×/d HSV; ganciclovir gel 0.15% 5×/d ×1 wk then tds; trifluridine 1% 9×/d; famciclovir 500 mg tds (HZO); valaciclovir 1 g tds HZO, 1–2 g tds ARN; valganciclovir 900 mg bd ×21 d induction then od (CMV).

cards.a: Vancomycin 1 mg/0.1 mL plus ceftazidime 2.25 mg/0.1 mL (or amikacin 0.4 mg).

chunks.title: Dyes, lubricants, hypertonic & anti-VEGF
chunks.tldr: Fluorescein: 1–2% drops/strips (defects, tonometry, CL fit), 10% IV (FFA). ICG IV (choroid). Lissamine green (devitalised cells, gentler) and rose bengal (stings). Lubricants: HPMC, carboxymethylcellulose, hyaluronate, PVA, carbomers, castor oil, paraffin; preservative-free for frequent use. Hypertonic: 5% NaCl drops/ointment, anhydrous glycerin (corneal oedema). Anti-VEGF intravitreal: aflibercept 2 mg/0.05 mL, bevacizumab 1.25 mg/0.05 mL (off-label), ranibizumab 0.5 mg/0.05 mL, pegaptanib 0.3 mg.

cards.q: Standard intravitreal doses of ranibizumab and aflibercept?
cards.a: Ranibizumab 0.5 mg/0.05 mL; aflibercept 2 mg/0.05 mL (bevacizumab 1.25 mg/0.05 mL).

chunks.title: Systemic drugs that harm the eye
chunks.tldr: IFIS (floppy iris): tamsulosin, alfuzosin, doxazosin, terazosin, silodosin, finasteride, also antipsychotics (risperidone, quetiapine, chlorpromazine), labetalol, donepezil. Angle closure: anticholinergics, adrenergics, TCAs, SSRIs (paroxetine), topiramate/acetazolamide/sulfonamides/zonisamide (ciliary effusion + myopic shift). Optic neuropathy: ethambutol, isoniazid, linezolid, amiodarone, disulfiram, chloramphenicol, cisplatin, docetaxel, PDE5 (NAION). Retinopathy: chloroquine/HCQ (bull's eye), thioridazine, tamoxifen (crystals), desferrioxamine, digoxin (yellow vision), quinine, interferon, linezolid. Vortex keratopathy: amiodarone, HCQ, indomethacin. IIH: tetracyclines, isotretinoin/vit A, levonorgestrel, nalidixic acid. Field loss: vigabatrin (monitor). Nystagmus/ocular motor: phenytoin, carbamazepine, lithium (downbeat), barbiturates. Steroids → glaucoma, PSC. Bisphosphonates → scleritis/uveitis. Sildenafil → blue tinge. Clofazimine crystals; phenothiazine pigment; warfarin in pregnancy → fetal anomalies.

cards.a: Ciliochoroidal effusion rotating the ciliary body forward (with myopic shift) — treat with stopping drug, cycloplegics, steroids; not iridotomy.

chunks.title: Systemic & local effects of eye drops; how to instil
chunks.tldr: Topical β-blockers: ~80% absorbed via nasal mucosa → bypasses liver first-pass; infant levels up to 6× oral; poor CYP2D6 metabolisers (8% whites, 24% blacks) at risk — bronchospasm, bradycardia/heart block, depression, impotence, MG worsening. Take cardiorespiratory history. Others: anticholinergics (delirium), phenylephrine (hypertension, arrhythmia, SAH), pilocarpine (cholinergic — sweating, GI, bronchospasm), long-acting anticholinesterases, chloramphenicol (marrow), steroids (Cushing). Local: anaesthetic abuse, preservative (BAK) keratopathy & pseudopemphigoid (also pilocarpine, timolol, antivirals), neomycin allergy, PGA changes, apraclonidine/brimonidine follicular reactions. Technique: one drop into pulled-down lower fornix, look up, avoid tip contact; close eyes; punctal occlusion ≥2 min; wait 10 min between drugs; ointment last. Report to the National Registry of Drug-Induced Ocular Side Effects.
chunks.hook: Press the inner corner for two minutes — less in the blood, more in the eye.

cards.q: Why are topical β-blockers more dangerous systemically than expected?
cards.a: Absorption through nasal mucosa delivers drug directly to the circulation, avoiding hepatic first-pass metabolism.
